events.title: Civic Literacy: Vocabulary for Voting
events.description: Learn vocabulary to help you vote! Together we will: Read an Easy Voter Guide for the November 2026 California General Election. Define important words and civic concepts. Understand the propositions on the ballot. Oct. 6: Intro to General Election & Offices; Oct. 20: Tax Propositions (Prop 40, 41, 42, 43); Oct. 22: Bonds & Tax Propositions (Prop 1, 2, 3, 37, 38); Oct. 27: Elections & Agencies (Prop 4, 5, 39, 44, 45). These workshops are an opportunity to practice reading, learn about American civics, build your English vocabulary, and prepare for voting in general elections. Free. Registration required. Presented in English.
events.blurb: Join online to read an Easy Voter Guide and learn the vocabulary behind this election's propositions.

events.title: Murder Mystery Theater
events.description: Step into the world of a mysterious mansion where one fateful evening takes a deadly turn. You'll be given a character to play, complete with secrets, suspicions, and motives of your own. As the story unfolds, clues will be revealed and everyone becomes a suspect. Work with your fellow guests to uncover hidden secrets, piece together the evidence, and determine who committed the murder before the mystery is solved. Will you crack the case, or will the murderer get away with it? No acting experience is necessary—just bring your imagination and your detective skills! Whether you're a seasoned sleuth or simply looking for a fun and theatrical evening, everyone has a role to play in this interactive murder mystery. For Grades 9-12. Registration required.
events.blurb: Take on a character role and hunt for clues as a mysterious mansion evening turns deadly.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club - Hillview
events.description: Join us to practice, build, and strengthen your English-speaking skills. This is a fun, welcoming and respectful environment for adult English learners. Club meetings are held weekly and led online by a trained facilitator. Our dedicated and experienced volunteer, Patricia, leads the program and will help you build confidence in your English-speaking abilities. Please be sure to register by clicking the Register button. By providing your email address, you will receive the Zoom meeting link before the program begins.
events.blurb: Practice speaking English with fellow adult learners in a weekly conversation club led by a trained facilitator.

events.title: Breathing & Meditation: The Natural Path to Better Immunity and Restful Sleep
events.description: Experience the soothing calm of meditation presented by library partner Art of Living Foundation. Enjoy this free, one-hour session focused on managing stress and anxiety through simple, evidence-based techniques. These sessions are open to all adults and include optional light physical movement, breathing practices, and guided meditation. No prior experience is necessary. The typical agenda for this one-hour session is as follows: Optional Yoga Stretches (10 minutes): Light, beginner-friendly stretches; Will be offered based on participant interest. Breathing Techniques (10 minutes): Guided practice of calming breathwork; Techniques that can be used daily to reduce stress. Guided Meditation (20 minutes): Deep relaxation and mindfulness practice; Designed to calm the mind and promote inner peace. Experience Sharing & Program Info (10 minutes): Participants may share experiences; Information about the Art of Living and wellness programs; Optional: 3-minute video clip of past participant testimonials (if AV is available). This program is geared to enrich the lives of adults and seniors. Registration is online.
events.blurb: Join this online session to learn simple breathing and meditation techniques for easing stress and sleeping better.

events.title: Afghan Cassette Archive: Stories, Sounds, and Music from Afghanistan
events.description: Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join Omid Jahan, founder of the Afghan Cassette Archive (@afghancassettearchive), for a multimedia listening session exploring Afghanistan's rich musical history through rare cassette recordings, archival materials, and personal stories. The program will highlight Afghan music from different eras and communities, including recordings preserved from Afghanistan and the Afghan diaspora. Attendees will have the opportunity to hear selections from the archive, learn about the stories behind the music and artists, and view original cassette tapes and other archival materials. The session offers a unique look at Afghan history, culture, migration, and memory through the music that has traveled across generations. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear rare cassette recordings and stories from the Afghan Cassette Archive's founder Omid Jahan.

events.title: Short Story Social: "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" by Jeanette Winterson
events.description: Love the idea of a book club but don't have time for a whole novel? Join our Short Story Social, a relaxed "book club" for short-story fans and busy readers. We meet virtually on the last Thursday of each month to discuss one or two contemporary short stories (no more than 40 pages total). Participate from anywhere—jump in late or leave early if needed! Registration is required to receive the Zoom meeting link. 2026 Reading List: June 25th - "The Shroud" in Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq; July 23rd - "Mall of America" by Suzanne Wang in The Best American Short Stories 2024; August 27th - "A Sunny Place for Shady People" in A Sunny Place for Shady People by Mariana Enriquez; September 24th - "Dominion" by Lauren Acampora in The Best American Short Stories 2025. * Also available in New England Review, Vol. 45, No. 2 - available through Gale Academic Onefile with your library card. October 29th - "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" in Night Side of the River by Jeanette Winterson
events.blurb: Discuss Jeanette Winterson's short stories "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" online with other quick-read fans in this casual book club.

events.title: A Taste of History: Remembering the Wine History of Mountain View
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Before Silicon Valley, before the apricot orchards, this region was wine country. From the first vines planted at Mission Santa Clara in 1798 to more than 100 wineries operating across Santa Clara County by the 1890s, the South Bay was once one of California's most productive wine regions. Join us for a presentation by fourth-generation Mountain View resident and museum professional Julie Bly De Vere. She will present a lively look at the winemakers, vineyards, and forgotten history that shaped our local landscape long before the tech industry arrived.
events.blurb: Hear the story of Mountain View's forgotten wine industry, from Mission Santa Clara's first vines to over 100 local wineries.

events.title: Mastering Medicare: Turn Confusion into Confidence
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join us for a free, beginner-focused educational session that explains Medicare parts, enrollment timelines, and coverage options. This is an opportunity to get expert insights and clarity on how the latest Medicare updates will affect you. Whether you're new to Medicare, nearing eligibility, or already enrolled, this seminar will help you understand everything you need to know to make informed decisions about your coverage. In this comprehensive discussion, we'll explore critical topics about Medicare, such as: The ABCs (and D): Breakdown of Part A (hospital), Part B (medical), Part C (Advantage), and Part D (prescription drugs). Eligibility & Timelines: Critical enrollment windows (like the Initial Enrollment Period) to avoid late penalties. Plan Comparisons: Differences between Original Medicare, Medicare Supplement (Medigap) insurance, and Medicare Advantage. Cost Management: Review of premiums, deductibles, and strategies to lower out-of-pocket expenses. Medicare Qualifications: An overview of the eligibility requirements for Medicare, including age, disability, and any other special conditions. Cost & Penalties: Information on Medicare premiums, deductibles, co-pays, and the penalties for late enrollment. Medicare vs. Employer coverage: How Medicare works alongside employer health insurance and when to consider enrolling in Medicare if you're still working. Don't miss out on this crucial opportunity to understand how Medicare will change in 2027 and how those changes impact you. Whether you're just starting to navigate Medicare or need a refresher, this seminar is designed for everyone! This workshop will be led by Claudette G. Klein. About the Presenter: Ms. Claudette G. Klein is the owner and CEO of Klein Financial Services, a full-service, financial services firm with a primary focus on health and wealth protection, and life coverage planning. She is a Certified Financial Planner with an exemplary track record in client care, honesty, reliability, commitment and dedication. With her industry expertise, she continues to be a steady source and adviser not only of her clients, but even those who simply desire to obtain a better and clearer understanding of health and life choices that can lead to security. With a reputation as a trusted financial advisor in the Bay Area for over thirty years, Ms. Claudette Klein continues to provide unmatched service and attention. She believes in always educating current and potential clients in creating strategies for their optimal benefit, helping them understand how to make sound financial choices, assisting them with strategies that can aid in reaching their personal plans and goals, along with the attainment of peace of mind for themselves and their families.
events.blurb: Hear a beginner-focused talk on Medicare parts, enrollment timelines, and coverage options at the library.

events.description: Therapy reading dogs provide a comforting presence for children as they navigate the exciting realm of books. This initiative aims to build confidence, enhance literacy skills and instill a lifelong love for reading. events.title: Sew Sew Saturday
events.description: Need a sewing machine? The Library has sewing machines (model: Baby Lock Joy) and a serger (model: Brother 1034D) that are available for use within the Library on a drop-in basis. events.title: Media, Information & AI Literacy: Navigating Our Changing Digital World
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. We live in an age of unprecedented access to information. But figuring out what to trust is becoming increasingly difficult. Social media algorithms shape what we see, headlines compete for our attention, and generative AI can now create remarkably convincing images, videos, and other content. In this interactive workshop, participants will build practical media and AI literacy skills for navigating this changing landscape. The workshop aims to help participants become critical thinkers and confident consumers of information and AI. About the Speaker: Tracy Wu is the founder of Meiflower, a Los Altos-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit focused on helping children, families, and communities develop the critical-thinking and digital-literacy skills needed to thrive in an increasingly technology-filled world. Tracy brings decades of corporate experience and a Master's degree in Finance. Most recently, she served as a Senior Program Manager in Platform Trust & Safety at LinkedIn, with experience related to online safety, platform integrity, and user trust. In the community, Tracy is also an Art Docent with the Los Altos School District and a reading tutor through the Santa Clara County Library District's Adult Literacy Program. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear a talk at Mountain View Public Library on spotting misinformation and sharpening your media and AI literacy skills.

events.title: Seed Packets Demystified
events.description: Seating is limited. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Do you love to look at seed catalogs and seed packets but wonder if you'd really be able to grow plants from seeds? Do you stare at the seed rack in your local nursery puzzling through what variety to plant and when you should plant it? Most seed packets contain a wealth of information to help you plant seeds of the right plant in the right place at the right time. But many of us don't bother reading the fine print, and jump straight to the planting. Join us for a lively discussion and analysis of how reading the fine print on your seed packets can help you be more successful in your garden. Infrared assistive listening systems are available for use during this event. Please see Library staff for assistance.
events.blurb: Learn how to read seed packets and catalogs so you can actually pick and grow the right varieties.

events.title: Amplify: Gatorbotics Gear Up!
events.description: Join us for a hands-on exploration of design thinking and engineering. Learn how to interview, brainstorm, and make as we build solutions to real problems we find in the world around us. Practice hands-on engineering and learn design thinking foundational skills. Walk away with your very own prototype and a newfound excitement for engineering! Hosted by Castilleja School's Robotics Team, Gatorbotics. Recommended Ages: 5-11. This event is part of Amplify: Teen Voices, a program for teens who want to share their interests and passions with an audience.
events.blurb: Build solutions to real-world problems while practicing hands-on engineering and design-thinking skills with Gatorbotics at the library.

events.title: Wild Fungi of California
events.description: Join Carrie Staller from Fork in the Path for an interactive hour of hands-on fun exploring the fascinating world of mushrooms! Learn how to identify mushrooms, discover chanterelles, morels, and porcini, and understand the difference between edible and poisonous varieties. We will have some specimens to touch and smell. This program is perfect for curious minds of all ages eager to learn about the natural world. About Fork in the Path: Fork in the Path offers forest-to-ocean-to-table learning programs for the adventurous of all ages across Northern California. We believe learning to forage and eating seasonal wild food is transformational. It helps us become more connected, whole, healthy, and happy. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear Carrie Staller explain how to identify mushrooms and tell edible species from poisonous ones.

events.title: Amplify: Mystery of the Human Brain
events.description: Have you ever wondered what's really going on in your head? The human brain is a weird, crazy, and fascinating thing, and most people (even adults!) barely understand it. In this interactive STEM event, teens from STEM Beyond Boundaries are going to help you explore the science behind memory, learning, dreams, and other cool stuff! Ages 8-13. This event is part of Amplify: Teen Voices, a program for teens who want to share their interests and passions with an audience.
events.blurb: Dig into how the human brain actually works through hands-on activities at Mountain View Public Library.

events.title: Coloring for Adults
events.description: Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Coloring sheets aren't just for kids! Come join us to unwind and color at the same time. You will be able to select from crayons, colored pencils, or markers to personalize your coloring sheet. Pencil in this moment of relaxation on your Sunday afternoon. This class is intended for adults, ages 18 and up only. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Pick up crayons, colored pencils, or markers and unwind with coloring sheets at the library.

events.title: Foundations for Artificial Intelligence
events.description: Curious about artificial intelligence and how it works? Join us for a free, beginner-friendly 60-minute session exploring the foundations of AI. Participants will learn how AI systems learn, where we encounter AI in everyday life, and how to use popular AI tools effectively. No previous AI or coding experience is required! This workshop is led by Together We AI, a nonprofit organization that aims to make AI education accessible to everyone.
events.blurb: Join online to learn how AI systems work and pick up tips for using popular AI tools.

events.title: Cookbook Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: October's theme is "cake or pie"! Each month we have a theme that you are free to interpret however you'd like. Choose a recipe to make from one of the many cookbooks or other resources in our collection — don't worry, we'll have plenty of suggestions for you! Then we'll meet to talk about books and cooking and enjoy each other's company. Photos of your finished dish are encouraged but not required. Are you Team Cake or Team Pie? Both? This month we'll be showing our team spirit by making either a cake or a pie, depending on which team you're on. You can make it sweet or savory, big enough for a crowd or small enough to be held in your hand — it's up to you! Think a Swedish smörgåstårta or a savory hand pie, or one of the many, many cupcake recipes available. Or if you really are Team Both, you might consider attempting the legendary cherpumple! Browse our incredible cookbook collection in the Library or our ebooks on Cloud Library or The Palace Project, find something that looks interesting to you, and cook! Come to our meeting ready to talk all about what you made and the book you used.
events.blurb: Make a cake or pie from a cookbook pick, then meet up to swap notes on this month's theme.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of The Mountains Sing by Nguyen Phan Que Mai. Multi-generational tale of the Tran family set against the backdrop of the Vietnam War. Vivid and steeped in the language and traditions of Vietnam, the book brings to life the human costs of the conflict from the point of view of the Vietnamese people themselves, while showing the true power of kindness and hope. A perfect follow-up to The Women (our Nov. selection), which brings to life the Vietnam War from an American perspective. The Monday Morning book club meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time.
events.blurb: Join the discussion of The Mountains Sing, a multi-generational Vietnam War saga, over coffee with fellow readers.

events.title: Informed Community Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for the Informed Community Book Club, a space dedicated to exploring and discussing pertinent social, economic, and political issues. If you are interested in participating in our democratic institutions or just making friends, join us! November's book will be The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future and What We Can Do About It, by Robert Weissman. From the publisher's website: Long-time corporate accountability crusaders Robert Weissman, Public Citizen president, and Joan Claybrook, Public Citizen president emeritus, investigate how giant corporations corrupt the policy-making process to block reforms favored by overwhelming majorities of the American people, and to enrich themselves through far-reaching corporate welfare schemes. The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future And What We Can Do About It pulls back the curtain on the hidden tactics that big corporations employ to have their way in Washington, D.C. and state capitols and city halls across the nation. The discussion will be hosted by former Los Gatos Planning Commissioner and current president of the Los Gatos Anti-Racism Coalition Jeff Suzuki.

events.title: Sound Bath Healing Meditation
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Gaby Castro-Moroder is back for another sound healing session! Come join us! Sound and music are used as a method of healing across various mediums. After being told for years that she has a healing presence, Gaby Castro started her sound healing journey and took certification courses in tuning forks, crystal sound bowls, and Tibetan sound bowls. Now she provides sound healing group and individual sessions under the name Song Pine and Stone, bringing her gentle presence to those in need. A group sound healing session runs about 60-90 minutes and includes the use of crystal sound healing bowls, Tibetan bowls, tuning forks, and various other sound healing instruments. Attendees will bring their own yoga mats, blankets, pillows, and whatever else they need to be comfortable during the session. Instruments will be played to create a sound bath and attendees will be encouraged to relax and enjoy the soft, soothing sounds. When the session ends, attendees will be asked to rehydrate and we'll discuss how the session felt for everyone. Age range: Adults and seniors. Note: A consent form may be required and provided at the event. Attendees need to consult with their physician and get approval to attend healing sessions if they have metal in their bodies, suffered concussions, have a pacemaker, use an insulin pump, and the like. If in doubt, consult your physician before the session. The Los Gatos Library recognizes the diversity of our community and is committed to accessibility for all patrons. We strive to make every visitor feel comfortable by ensuring equal access to programs, services, and activities. If you require a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in a library program, please contact library@losgatosca.gov
events.blurb: Lie back and let Gaby Castro-Moroder's sound healing session wash over you with music and instruments.

This will be our very first Cookbook Swap, and if everyone has a good time, we can look into making it a regular event. If you'd like, we'll have note cards for you to mark your favorite recipes in the books so their new owners will have a fun place to start.

events.description: Come join fellow needlework and textile arts enthusiasts at the library! Crafters of all levels are welcome to bring their projects and chat, teach, learn, and make new friends at this casual weekly get-together. This group is entirely self-directed and you are encouraged to bring your own tools and materials. If you are looking for some inspiration or don't know where to start, check out Creativebug - it's free with your library card and offers hundreds of project ideas and instructions.
events.blurb: Bring your needlework or textile project and stitch, chat, and swap tips with fellow crafters at the library.

events.title: Crafty Corner (Ages 3-10)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Take some time out of your afternoon to imagine and create! Join us for a crafty activity in the Children's Room. (Previously known as Tinker Tuesday.) This program is geared towards children ages 3 through ~10. This program takes place on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 pm in the Children's Room. Please note that in August, November, and December, there is only 1 Crafty Corner event during those months. Check our calendar for accurate up-to-date information.
events.blurb: Make a hands-on craft in the Children's Room with kids ages 3 through 10.

events.title: Creative Break
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Have you been wanting to start journaling or using a planner but can't find the time or space to do it at home? Take some time for creativity at the Library and journal, work on your planner, or draw in your sketchbook. We'll provide some inspiration and fun stationery like washi tape, stickers, stamps, and pens; you bring your journal, planner, sketchbook, etc. This is a drop-in program, so join us for 10 minutes if that's all you have, or stay for the whole time!
events.blurb: Settle in at the library to journal, plan, or sketch during this quiet creative session.

events.title: Storytime (Ages 0-5)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Early learners (babies and toddlers) and their families are welcome to join us at the Library for Storytime, where we will wiggle, sing, read, and dance together! Our program is developmentally appropriate for ages 0-5, and our goal is to create memories and special bonds between caregivers and their children, and to help with building skills for school readiness and for a future of loving books!
events.blurb: Wiggle, sing, read, and dance with your little one at this Library storytime for babies and toddlers.

events.title: Facing Reality Without Losing Your Peace of Mind
events.description: We live in a time of extraordinary uncertainty and change. Political turmoil, economic instability, and troubling world events can leave us feeling anxious, overwhelmed, or helpless. Explore how to remain engaged with the world while preserving our inner peace. We may not be able to control what's happening around us, but we can learn to meet it without losing our center.
events.blurb: Hear a talk on staying engaged with a turbulent world while protecting your own inner peace.

events.title: Bug Power with Beetlelady! (Ages 6-12)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Register to join in on this artistic and heroic exploration of bugs with Dr. Stephanie Dole, also known as Beetlelady! Learn all about different types of insects by interacting with live bugs, and invent your own superhero bug with a fun drawing activity! This class is for ages 6-12, and registration is required (registration opens 3 weeks prior to the event).
events.blurb: Meet live insects and invent your own bug superhero with Beetlelady in this hands-on drawing activity.

events.title: Free Repairs with Repair Café
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Do you need help repairing something? Repair Café Silicon Valley will be at the library offering free repairs on household items such as toasters, lamps, radios, clothing, bikes, and more. Limit two items per household; last repairs accepted at 2:30 PM. Visit repaircafesv.org for more information about their mission and to see when other events are scheduled.
events.blurb: Bring a broken toaster, lamp, radio, or bike and get it fixed free by Repair Café Silicon Valley volunteers.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of Felicia's Journey by William Trevor. A story of lost opportunities, naivety, and misplaced hopes of an Irish girl who leaves Ireland to find her boyfriend in England. By one of Ireland's most admired writers. The Monday Morning book club meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time.
events.blurb: Discuss Felicia's Journey, William Trevor's story of an Irish girl chasing lost hopes in England, with the group.

events.title: Cafecito Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: This book club reads exclusively Spanish books and meets on the 2nd Thursday of every month from 10-11 AM in the library's conference room (1st Floor). Este club de lectura lee libros exclusivamente en español y se reúne el segundo jueves de cada mes de 10 a 11 a.m. en la sala de conferencias de la biblioteca (primer piso).
events.blurb: Discuss a Spanish-language book with fellow readers in the library's first-floor conference room.

events.title: Psychic Readings
events.description: Gather your friends for a pre-Halloween evening of psychic readings with Psychic Medium Janis Manacsa and Sound Practitioner Julie Kalua. Experience live gallery readings, opening and closing sound baths, and the mystery of the season. October 30, 6:30–9 p.m. at East West Bookshop. Limited to 20 guests.
events.blurb: Get a live gallery reading from a psychic medium and settle into sound baths with a sound practitioner.

We meet in the 2nd-floor Tech Lab, and a clipboard for signing up is at the 2nd-floor reference desk starting at 2:30 PM.

events.title: Existence Beyond Death: With Dr. Seng-Beng Ho - Friday November 6th at 7pm
events.description: Explore near-death experiences, reincarnation, and the UFO connection with author and cognitive scientist Dr. Seng-Beng Ho. An evening of research, reported experiences, and questions about consciousness and reality, followed by Q&A. November 6, 7–8:30 p.m. | $25.
events.blurb: Hear cognitive scientist Dr. Seng-Beng Ho discuss near-death experiences, reincarnation, and consciousness, then join the Q&A.

events.title: Seed Library Tabling
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a fun-filled craft in the lobby that promotes the Los Gatos Seed Library. Learn more about community stewardship and how to collect and donate seeds, along with why native plants are so important to our community health and wellbeing.
events.blurb: Make a craft in the library lobby while learning how to collect and donate seeds for the Los Gatos Seed Library.

events.title: Park-It Market
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join the team from West Valley Community Services for their twice-monthly Park-It Market. On the second and fourth Thursday of each month, WVCS offers free access to food including fresh produce, meat, dairy products, dry goods and canned food.
events.blurb: Pick up free fresh produce, meat, dairy, and canned goods from West Valley Community Services.

events.title: Adventure Skeletons TTRPG
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a Halloween-themed role-playing game, Adventure Skeletons. Players will make their way through the haunted Spirit Halloween to... Liberate their skeleton kin? Take over the world? Go on vacation? The choice is yours!

This event is free to attend. We look forward to seeing you on the Row!

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) 502: Listening & Speaking
events.description: ESL Listening & Speaking 1 - This is a non-credit, high-beginning level ESL course. Students will learn to pronounce basic words accurately, communicate effectively, understand and use basic grammar structures, and build their foundational vocabulary. To Enroll, You Must: Complete and pass the Self-Guided Computer Assessment. This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. To ensure accurate results, the GSP should be completed independently and in a quiet setting, without assistance from others. Submit the registration form. To schedule your assessment appointment, send an email to marcela.guevara@sjlibrary.org. ESL 502 Course Information: Starts: August 25, 2026; Ends: December 10, 2026; Class Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday; Time: 5:15 PM – 6:45 PM; Instructor: TBD. We will assist you with the application and registration processes in person at the Educational Park Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: We will assist you with the application and registration processes in person at the Educational Park Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice pronunciation, basic grammar, and vocabulary in this high-beginning ESL listening and speaking class.

events.title: TeenTober: Successfully Navigating College Admissions Watch Party + Stickering Activity
events.description: Learn about how to successfully navigate college admissions this fall. Destress by doing a stickering activity and socializing with teens in your community after. Snacks provided. While supplies last. Free. No registration required. For teens (ages 13-18). Explore additional activities and resources available to teens through Teen Tober. Wednesday 09/30 (5 PM-6 PM): Patelco: Smart Money Moves; Thursday 10/01 – Saturday 10/31: Teen Tober Bingo (pick up a Bingo sheet in the Teen Room); Wednesday 10/07 (5 PM-6:30 PM): Paint a Glow-in-the-Dark-Jar or Tote Bag; Wednesday 10/14 (5 PM-6 PM): Challenged Books Kahoot / Bingo; Wednesday 10/21 (4:30 PM-6 PM): Successfully Navigating College Admissions Watch Party + Stickering Activity; Wednesday 10/28 (5 PM-6 PM): In-Person Library Scavenger Hunt.
events.blurb: Watch a session on navigating college admissions, then decorate stickers and chat with other teens.

events.title: Intro to Ukulele for Adults
events.description: In this 3-part series for adults, participants will learn the basics of playing the ukulele, will acquire the ability to read chords, get hands-on experience with the instrument, and learn some rudimentary concepts of music theory. The series will include 3 sessions, and each session will cover the following: Session 1 (10/14): Chords & how to read them; How to hold & strum the ukulele; Tuning; Session 2 (10/21): Review chords & introduce 3-finger chords; Introduce rhythm patterns. Session 3 (10/28): Practicing rhythm patterns; putting it all together; advanced techniques. No musical experience required. Ukuleles will be provided to participants, but you may bring your own if you have one. Registration is required. Registration opens in September and closes the day before the first session. Limited to 10 seats. Join the waitlist if the registration is filled. We recommend that participants come to all three sessions.
events.blurb: Learn basic ukulele chords, strumming, and music theory basics in this hands-on adult series.

events.title: Baby Lap-Sit Story Time
events.description: This program is geared for pre-walking children and their parents or caregivers. Baby Lap-Sit Storytime invites newborns, infants, and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. The program includes 20-25 minutes of stories and songs, followed by 40 minutes of open play with age-appropriate toys. All attendees will be required to observe the library's Safety Guidelines. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Bring your pre-walking baby to listen to stories and rhymes built for little ones.

events.title: Family Storytime + Stay & Play
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents / caregivers! After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! Until 6:30 pm the Storytime librarian and special toys will be on the Children's Room floor to keep the fun going. Meet new friends, play with toys, chat, get book recommendations, and maybe even create something! Storytime: 5:30-6:00 PM; Stay & Play: 6:00-6:30 PM. Free, with limited capacity. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime.
events.blurb: Join stories, songs, rhymes, and movement activities with the whole family at Stay & Play storytime.

events.title: Vineland's Evening Book Club
events.description: Grab a book and meet some new friends! Our monthly evening book club meets on the third Wednesday of every month to discuss a fiction book. Newcomers welcome! Our upcoming selections are: October: The Tenant by Freida McFadden; November: The Library Book by Susan Orlean; December: These Summer Storms by Sarah MacLean; January: The Correspondent by Virginia Evans; February: Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen. Be sure to let us know if you have any suggestions for future book selections! We vote on future book choices every few months. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Meet fellow readers to discuss this month's chosen fiction title over evening conversation.

events.title: TeenHQ Custom Keychains
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Middle and high school students are welcome to join us for creating custom keychains or charms. Create your own personalized acrylic or wooden keychain by drawing it out on paper, then scanning it with our Glowforge and getting it engraved and cut (print) out while you watch. Alternatively, pick a black & white image to engrave into your keychain or add custom text. Supplies are limited to 1 single-sided keychain per participant. Please Note: You can bring a prepared design in advance. Be sure that your design is black on white paper and there isn't shading. On average, a maximum of 8 teens can create a custom keychain or charm during this program. This program tends to take the entire hour and a half time period as it can take anywhere between 5 and 15 minutes to cut each keychain, based on complexity. Please be prepared to stay the entire length of the program to wait for your keychain. This program is free. No pre-registration required. This program is specifically for Middle and High Schoolers. Adult caregivers and younger siblings will be asked to sit in the Teen Reading Room while they wait.
events.blurb: Design and cut your own acrylic or wooden keychain using the library's Glowforge laser engraver.

events.title: One-On-One Tech Help (English or Tiếng Việt)

They can assist you with basic tech issues, such as: Setting up an email account, composing & sending emails, using email attachments; Web searches and basic data entry; Learning the basics of Microsoft Word and Excel and web-based productivity software such as Google Docs; Using the library's pay-for-print and photocopy machines; Downloading apps on your phone or tablet; And much more! You are welcome to bring your own device, such as a laptop, phone or tablet, or you can use one of our computers. Free. No registration required.
events.attendanceNote: Drop-ins subject to availability.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) - ESL 501: Reading & Writing 1
events.description: Develop your English language skills by practicing speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Do you want to build your English language skills and your confidence? This beginning non-credit ESL course is free! ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1. What will you learn in this class? This is a non-credit, high-beginning-level integrated ESL skills course emphasizing basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will learn to comprehend frequently used words in context, use learned phrases and sentences to express ideas in basic writing, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified material. Course Information: Starts: August 25, 2026; Ends: December 10, 2026; Meeting Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday; Time: 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM; Instructor: Michelle N. Henninger. Before the classes start, you must complete a Guided Self-Placement (GSP). This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. We will assist you with the application and registration process in person at the Edenvale Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Build your English reading, writing, and speaking skills in this free beginning ESL class at Edenvale Library.

events.title: Readers' Book Club
events.description: Join our Readers' Book Club to share the joy of reading and to expand your reading horizons. We will read thought-provoking adult fiction of various genres for readers of different ages and backgrounds. For the remaining months, we will read: Their Eyes Were Watching God by Zora Neale Hurston; The Teacher of Nomad Land by Daniel Nayeri. What to expect: For October, we will be reading Their Eyes Were Watching God by Zora Neale Hurston, who tells the story of Janie Crawford, in Black dialect. events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) 502: Listening & Speaking
events.description: ESL Listening & Speaking 1 - This is a non-credit, high-beginning level ESL course. Students will learn to pronounce basic words accurately, communicate effectively, understand and use basic grammar structures, and build their foundational vocabulary. To Enroll, You Must: Complete and pass the Self-Guided Computer Assessment. This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. events.title: Inventing Rules for AI: Read + Learn + Craft
events.description: Join us for the 2nd installment of "Crafting Our Future" as we explore a different kind of science fiction: AI behavioral rulebooks. We will read excerpts from Anthropic's Claude's Constitution and OpenAI's Model Spec as stories that imagine how an AI system should work, what kind of interactions with end users the system expects, and when it should refuse a request. "Inventing the Rules of AI" will host Dr. Nada Madkour, Director of the AI Security Initiative at UC Berkeley's Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity. Dr. Madkour is an expert in writing and evaluating frameworks that govern how emerging technologies are safely and securely designed, implemented, deployed, and maintained. Dr. Madkour will guide us through the key security and privacy challenges unique to AI systems, from data protection to companionship and manipulation. We'll spend time imagining what rules and behaviors we would write for emerging technologies after considering the aspirations for the system imagined in the behavioral rules written by frontier AI companies. As with every session in the series, we turn from reading and learning to crafting our individual and collective visions for the future through quilting, drawing or writing. Individual contributions will be collected and turned into a vibrant patchwork exhibit. Don't miss this chance to help craft a tangible representation of the future we envision and what emerging technologies should look like for our community in San José and beyond. Registration is required. Light snacks will be provided. Dr. Sarah Papazoglakis is the Library's Technologist-in-Residence. She is a humanist and technologist who holds a PhD in Literature from the University of California, Santa Cruz. She has dedicated almost a decade to designing ethical frameworks for building technology responsibly, emphasizing how storytelling and fiction are common foundations of both literature and emerging technologies like AI. "Crafting Our Future" is a year-long community conversation series that will foster thoughtful discussions around emerging technologies using texts, film, and art as a shared point of reference.
events.blurb: Read and discuss AI behavioral rulebooks, then craft your own as part of this Willow Glen Library series.

events.title: AI for Small Business: Boost Sales and Automate Your Workflow
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: SCORE Silicon Valley supports entrepreneurs and small business owners throughout Santa Clara and San Mateo Counties with free, expert mentoring and practical guidance to launch, scale, and innovate. This hands-on workshop demystifies AI for small business owners, showing them how to apply it directly to sales, customer capture, and operations starting the same day. The session features two SCORE Silicon Valley mentors leading live, demo-driven instruction. Attendees will watch AI tools applied in real time, with every prompt and workflow included in take-home materials so they can replicate the work on their own businesses immediately. Session 1: Boost Your Sales by Leveraging AI — Vinay Murthy. Vinay Murthy is a SCORE Silicon Valley mentor with over 30 years in technology and software, including leadership roles at AWS, Google, YouTube, and 8x8, and two startups he founded. He covers: How AI assistants decide which businesses to recommend, and the levers owners control; How AI receptionists and booking chat capture calls and inquiries that would otherwise be lost; How AI shopping agents evaluate products and services, and why unclear pricing or service details make a business invisible to them; Setting up automated welcome, follow-up, and win-back messages that run without ongoing effort; A prioritized action list tailored to online stores, storefronts, consulting practices, and small B2B companies. Session 2: Working Smarter: Automate Your Business with AI — Andrew Apodaca. Andrew Apodaca is a SCORE Silicon Valley mentor whose background spans automation, marketing, and analytics at Apple, Adobe, and Zendesk. He covers: Capture: AI-powered forms and chat that qualify and route leads the moment they arrive; Automate: Follow-up and re-engagement sequences that run without manual work; Measure: Turning existing sales and marketing data into a live dashboard to see what's working. Together, the two sessions give small business owners a practical, end-to-end view of how to use AI to win more customers, retain them, and make faster, data-driven decisions — with tools they can start using immediately. Parking validation for garage at 88 S. 4th Street will be provided at the program.
events.blurb: Learn from SCORE mentors how small businesses can use AI to boost sales and automate workflows at King Library.

events.title: Author Event: Book launch for Bruce Overby's latest novel
events.description: Join us for an evening with local writer Bruce Overby (The Cyclone Release and recently released Tristan 4 America) with Geri Spieler (Housewife Assassin, Regina of Warsaw) serving as moderator. Bruce Overby is a fiction writer with particular interest in issues of loss and belonging, family and relationships, the human condition in a technology-driven world, and addiction. His fiction has appeared in Storyglossia, the Green Mountains Review, the Evening Street Review, and the anthology Home of the Brave: Stories in Uniform from Press53. "Bookmarks," the story of a brother's struggle with alcoholism, his love of poetry, and the sometimes disturbing mix of the two, won first prize in the Lorian Hemingway Short Story Competition. Bruce's debut novel, The Cyclone Release, was a finalist in the Blue Moon Novel Competition and is available now from Madville Publishing. His second novel, Tristan 4 America, is forthcoming from Willow River Press in October 2026. Bruce is a graduate of the MFA in Writing Program at Queens University of Charlotte. A San Jose native, Bruce is a member of California Writers Club-SF Peninsula Branch and participated in Rinconada Library's inaugural book fair in April. Books will be available for purchase. Bring your questions!

Lưu ý: Chương trình tập trung hỗ trợ các câu hỏi và thao tác công nghệ cơ bản. Chào đón quý vị tới gặp nhân viên thư viện nếu có câu hỏi đơn giản. Cách thức ghi danh: Xin ghi danh đặt hẹn trước (thư viện sẽ ưu tiên cho người có lịch hẹn): Gọi điện thoại: (408) 808-3060. Hoặc gửi email cho cô Rebecca Quan: rebecca.quan@sjlibrary.org Hosted by Evergreen Branch. #dsb Digital Skills

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: Berryessa Branch Library presents an in-person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English speaking & conversation skills used in everyday settings. All levels of English-speaking skills are welcome! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice your English conversation skills with other learners in a welcoming club setting.

events.title: Sphero Robots: Open Workshop + Lessons
events.description: Intended for students 5+ years old. Students will be using Sphero Robots + Sphero Apps + iPads to control their robots and program and code activities. Parents, caregivers, and siblings welcome. This will be an open workshop meaning you can just mess around with the robot via the draw or block coding options or follow a lesson in the app and code it to do something. This robotics class is beginner-friendly and suitable for younger ages. An instructor and/or volunteers will be available for help. Some obstacles, tape, ramps, etc. will be available; feel free to bring your own obstacles to maneuver around. Free. No registration required. 15 Robots available: Drop-in okay; first-come, first-served. Some people leave early, some people come late. Come one time, or come weekly; it's up to you!
events.attendanceNote: Free. No registration required. 15 robots available: Drop-in okay; first-come, first-served. Some people leave early, some people come late. Come one time, or come weekly, up to you!

events.title: Village Square Branch Monthly Teens Reach Meeting
events.description: Learn about volunteering at the library! This leadership and volunteer service group for teens ages 13-18 meets on the fourth Friday in October. Get involved, earn volunteer hours, and be a leader in the library. To become a member of Village Square's Teens Reach to volunteer, you must be 13-18 years of age, have a strong interest in the library, enjoy working with people of all ages and cultures, be reliable and communicative, and be willing to learn new skills. Membership requires regular attendance at meetings, participation in and support of library activities and events, and a sense of fun and adventure. As a bonus, Teens Reach members can earn community service hours through participation in meetings and other volunteer opportunities. For more information and to apply to volunteer go to www.sjpl.org/teensReach or email at aasia.ali@sjlibrary.org.
events.blurb: Join teens to learn about library volunteering, earn service hours, and build leadership skills.

events.title: Friday Family Game Zone
events.description: Looking for a fun way to unwind on a Friday afternoon? C'mon over to our weekly Friday Family Game Zone. In addition to board games and card games, we'll have our Nintendo Switch hooked up for attendees to play Mario Kart, Super Smash Bros., Super Mario Party, and more. Free. No registration is required. This program is great for kids ages 4 to 17 as well as their families and caregivers. Most events will take place in the Community Room. The Friday, September 18 event will take place in the Teen Room. Viernes de Juegos en Familia ¿Buscas una forma divertida de relajarte el viernes por la tarde? ¡Ven a nuestros Viernes de Juegos en Familia! Además de juegos de mesa y de cartas, tendremos nuestra Nintendo Switch lista para que los asistentes jueguen Mario Kart, Super Smash Bros. y Super Mario. No se requiere inscripción previa. Este programa es ideal para niños y niñas de 4 a 17 años, así como para sus familias y cuidadores. Acompáñanos mientras jugamos a títulos de éxito para Nintendo Switch, como Super Mario Brothers Party, Mario Kart, Super Smash Bros. y más. También tenemos juegos de mesa y juegos de cartas para niños, adolescentes y familias. Gratis. No se necesita inscribirse. Recomendado para edades de 4 a 17 años y familias / cuidadores. La mayoría de los eventos se llevarán a cabo en la Sala Comunitaria. El evento del viernes 18 de septiembre tendrá lugar en la Sala para Adolescentes.
events.blurb: Play board games, card games, and Mario Kart on the Switch at this weekly Friday game gathering.

events.title: ESL Workforce Development Workshop - Day 4: Interview Skills & Answering Questions
events.description: Join us for a five-session workshop designed for ESL learners who want to strengthen their workplace communication skills. In addition, participants will develop basic digital skills by learning how to use Google Workspace tools (Docs, Slides, and Drive) and Canva to create professional documents and presentations that can support job searches, interviews, and career advancement. Participants should be able to communicate in basic English (speaking, reading, and writing). Workshop Topic: Interview Skills & Answering Questions. This is a free program. Registration is required. Talleres de Desarrollo Laboral para Estudiantes Hispanos de ESL. Acompáñenos a este taller de cinco sesiones diseñado para estudiantes de inglés (ESL) que desean fortalecer sus habilidades de comunicación en el entorno laboral. Además, los participantes desarrollarán habilidades digitales básicas al aprender a utilizar las herramientas de Google Workspace (Docs, Slides y Drive) y Canva para crear documentos y presentaciones profesionales que les apoyen en la búsqueda de empleo, las entrevistas y el desarrollo de su carrera profesional. Los participantes deben tener la capacidad de comunicarse en inglés a un nivel básico (hablar, leer y escribir). Tema del taller: Habilidades para Entrevistas y Cómo Responder Preguntas. Este programa es Gratuito. Es necesario registrarse.
events.blurb: Practice interview questions and workplace communication skills in this ESL workshop session on interview strategies.

events.title: Asistencia tecnológica y ayuda personalizada
events.description: ¿Estás cansado de no poder hacer cosas tecnológicas por ti mismo? ¿Cansado de esperar a que los miembros de tu familia te ayuden o hagan las cosas por ti? ¡Ahora puedes aprender a hacer todo eso por ti mismo! Tenemos personas pacientes y serviciales disponibles para ayudarte a aprender cualquier tema relacionado con la tecnología. Nunca es tarde para aprender a usar la tecnología. ¡Solo llámanos! La biblioteca te brindará apoyo para: Abrir una cuenta de correo electrónico; Conectarse a un hotspot / Wi-Fi; Usar Chromebooks / computadoras; Usar Zoom; Encontrar e inscribirse en clases de la biblioteca; Obtener una tarjeta de la biblioteca; Reservar materiales; Usar aplicaciones de la biblioteca; Teléfono móvil; Busca en internet. Este es un programa presencial organizado en la Sucursal de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana. El personal de la biblioteca o un voluntario estarán allí para guiarte en todo, pero serás tú quien controle la computadora. Si no puede asistir a su cita, llame y cancele. Se dará prioridad a los clientes que no falten a sus citas. Gratis. Se requiere registro. Para registrarse, llame al (408) 294-1237.
events.blurb: Get personalized tech help at Biblioteca Latinoamericana and learn to handle everyday tech tasks on your own.

events.title: Reading Buddies
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades TK-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a trained volunteer or staff member. Reading Buddies creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our volunteers will listen to children read and provide support in phonics, sight words, and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the Rose Garden Branch Library. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating students.
events.attendanceNote: Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating students.
events.blurb: Pair up with a trained volunteer to read one-on-one and build reading confidence.

events.title: Cricut Open Lab
events.description: The Cricut Open Lab is a 45-minute learning session on select Fridays with machines available to use. First-time users can learn what the Cricut machine is and how it works. You can also watch these tutorial videos ahead of time to get a better idea of how to use the Cricut machine and Design Space. For those who already have experience using Cricut, they are welcome to register to use a machine independently to cut out their designs. We will have Cricut machines (Explore/Air and Maker), limited supplies, and several designs available for participants. Individuals or groups up to 3 people can register for the program. Registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Vineland Branch Library.
events.blurb: Try out the library's Cricut machines and learn the basics in a 45-minute open lab session.

events.title: AnatoKidz
events.description: Join us at the Alviso Branch Library for some fun and interactive anatomy lessons designed just for kids! Explore the brain, heart, lungs, bones, and more in a fun and engaging way with activities that will boost your curiosity, confidence, and critical thinking. This is a 4-part series. Participants may come to the sessions that interest them or even all: October 2: The Brain & Nervous System; October 9: The Digestive System; October 16: Respiratory; October 23: Skeletal & Muscular. Recommended for Children ages 5 - 10. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bring the kids to explore interactive anatomy activities covering the brain, heart, lungs, and bones.

events.title: Knit-Alongs
events.description: Starting Time: 2:30 pm; Ending Time: 4:00 pm; Community Room 201A. On the first Friday of each month we will meet in Room 201B. Cupertino Library Knit Alongs continue in 2026! All adult knitters and crocheters are welcome. No registration or sign-up required. We're always happy to meet someone new, so please feel free to join us. Meet new friends, start a new project, or finish an old one. Please note: This is mostly a social group for knitters and crocheters aged 18 and older. It is not intended to be a class for regular knitting and crochet instruction. We can supply some knitting and crochet supplies, but everyone is encouraged to bring their own knitting needles, crochet hooks and yarn. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Bring your needles or hook and knit or crochet alongside fellow adults at Cupertino Library's Knit-Along.

It is a wonderful opportunity for both children and parents to socialize while enjoying a fresh cup of coffee. This program is designed for families with children ages 0–5. No registration required but space is limited. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.attendanceNote: No registration required but space is limited.

events.title: Genealogy Lab
events.description: Come to the Los Altos Library to work on your current family history research project in the company of other genealogy hobbyists. Bring whatever you need for your work (e.g. computer, reference materials, notebook). While this is not an instructional session, you can get peer support for questions as well as access to the library's genealogy collection, including Ancestry and other databases. Sessions at 10 a.m.-noon on the 2nd and 4th Fridays of most months September through June. Hosted by volunteers from the Los Altos Chapter, Daughters of the American Revolution. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Bring your family history research and work alongside fellow genealogy hobbyists for peer support.

events.title: Family Coloring
events.description: Drop in for an afternoon of coloring for the whole family! Coloring pages with various themes, designs, and levels of complexity can be enjoyed by patrons of all ages. For little ones, coloring and drawing improve fine motor skills, encourage focus, and nurture creativity. For teens and adults, coloring can reduce stress and improve mental health. Come in to color! If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: Knit & Crochet Circle
events.description: Do you love to knit and/or crochet? Join us on Friday afternoons for our knit and crochet circle. events.description: Join us for Falun Dafa classes provided by the Classical Arts Foundation. Relieve stress and anxiety; Increase energy and vitality; Improve physical health. events.title: Learn English: Beyond the Basics
events.description: English as a Second Language (ESL) / Learn English: Beyond the Basics is an in-person 7-week class with lessons on English grammar, pronunciation, and idioms. It is for adult (18 years and older) intermediate and advanced English learners who can have a conversation in English and want to improve their pronunciation and understanding. To register for the entire 7-week series, please include your email address and make sure it is entered correctly. Please register only once for the entire series. Registration closes on the 3rd week of class.
events.blurb: Practice English grammar, pronunciation, and idioms in this in-person class for intermediate and advanced adult learners.

events.title: Asistencia para Búsqueda de Trabajo
events.description: ¿Buscas apoyo para avanzar en tu carrera? ¡Estamos aquí para ayudarte! Ofrecemos asistencia Gratuita en: Creación de Resume y Carta de Presentación - Destaca tus habilidades y experiencia con documentos profesionales que abran puertas. Búsqueda de Oportunidades de Empleo - Te guiamos para encontrar vacantes en los principales sitios web de trabajo. Llenado de Formularios de Solicitud - Incluye ayuda con verificación de historial laboral, y otros documentos esenciales para tu contratación; Técnicas y Consejos para Entrevistas - Aprende cómo responder con confianza, qué decir, qué evitar y cómo causar una excelente impresión. Práctica para el Examen Escrito de Manejo - Prepárate con materiales y preguntas de práctica para aprobar tu examen.
events.attendanceNote: De martes a sábado. Por cita únicamente. Por favor contactar a Marlene Sanchez por correo, marlene.sanchez@sjlibrary.org o teléfono, 408.808.3033 para agendar su cita.
events.blurb: Get free help at Hillview Library building a strong resume and cover letter for your job search.

events.title: Music and Movement
events.description: Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents / caregivers! Free, 50-person maximum. Story Time tickets required. Another event, Music and Movement B, will start at 11:15 for those that weren't able to make it inside for this event. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. events.title: 1 on 1 Tech Assistance
events.description: Do you need to brush up your computer skills? Whether you need assistance putting together a Word document, Excel spreadsheet, or PowerPoint presentation, submitting an online job application or other government document, or learning a new online tool, our experienced and dedicated tech tutors can help! Current Weekly Schedule: Wednesdays at 4:00 PM (in the Internet Cafe); Thursdays at 11 AM - assistance available in English or Mandarin Chinese (in the Group Study Room); Saturdays at 10 AM (in the Group Study Room). How To Attend: Participants are encouraged to pre-register; however, drop-ins are also considered.
events.blurb: Sit down one-on-one with a tech tutor to get help sharpening your computer skills.

events.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines
events.description: Every now and then, libraries need a little extra love from the communities they serve. You can volunteer away your library fines at a rate of $20 per hour while helping the library maintain a clean and welcoming environment. Volunteers will be responsible for: Book cover cleaning – Use disinfecting wipes to reinvigorate dingy books. Bookshelves – Dust shelves and organize library materials. Deep cleaning computers – Use disinfecting wipes to disinfect computer mice and mouse pads and compressed air to remove any dust particles or debris. Material inspection – Check books for torn pages, pen marks, etc. This is a perfect opportunity for anyone interested in volunteering away their library fines. Details and Requirements: Must be able to commit to the full session; Anyone under the age of 15 must volunteer alongside a parent / guardian; No experience or special skills necessary; Training and supplies will be provided. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Please register online or ask for assistance by calling/visiting our Information Desk. Space is limited.
events.blurb: Work off your library fines by volunteering to help keep the Alviso Library clean and welcoming.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer. Pre-registration is not required, and children may drop in to hear a story any time during the program. This program is best suited for preschoolers and children in grades K-3 and will be held in the Reading to Children corner, within the Children's Area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bring your child to hear a volunteer read aloud in a small group at Berryessa Library.

events.title: Growing Great Garlic and Shallots
events.description: While the rest of the garden slows down, garlic and shallots are just getting started! These culinary powerhouses grow beautifully in our local winter conditions. UC Master Gardener Aparna Bugwadia will guide you through the essentials of a productive season, including proper soil preparation, planting depths, and the patient art of harvesting and curing. Come discover how easy it is to keep your pantry stocked with homegrown flavor! You'll learn how to select the best varieties for the Bay Area, nurture your soil for peak flavor, and master the timing for planting, curing, and storing your harvest. Presented by the UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Learn tips for growing garlic and shallots during the cooler months at the Rose Garden Library.

events.title: Job Interview Coaching for Adults & Teens
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: You applied for a job and received a call back for an interview. Congratulations! Do you want help preparing for the interview? Meet one-on-one with Daniel, an experienced job interview coach, to help you prepare by giving feedback on your resume and conducting a mock interview. Sessions are one hour in length. Be prepared to share things with Daniel such as a current resume, the job position description you applied for, and if you can, come dressed as if you were going into the actual interview. You must register for this event and registration ends the Thursday before the program. If you registered successfully, you will get a registration confirmation email with a link to pick your choice of time for this Saturday's program. Each session is one hour (15-30 minutes for interviewing + 30-45 minutes for helpful feedback). The one-hour time slots to pick from are as follows: 10:00 - 11:00 am or 11:00 am - 12:00 pm. Please note that there is a 5-minute buffer to include any setup and help prevent any overlap between appointments. Resumes and job position descriptions are reviewed in advance. Please email documents to Jeff.Tibayan@sjlibrary.org by 5 PM on the Thursday before your Saturday session. This gives Daniel enough time to prepare job interview materials. Registration Information: Please register using a valid email address. Double-check that your email address is correct before confirming your registration.
events.blurb: Meet one-on-one with a coach for resume feedback and a mock job interview.

events.title: Athena Project
events.description: Spark curiosity and discover the joy of learning with the Athena Project! This interactive enrichment program for students in grades 2–5 combines the principles of classical education with hands-on activities that bring mathematics, language arts, history, science, and literature to life. Through games, crafts, experiments, storytelling, role-play, and collaborative projects, participants will strengthen critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and communication skills while exploring new ideas in a supportive and engaging environment. Every session is designed to inspire confidence, curiosity, and a lifelong love of learning. Ages: 7-11 (2nd grade to 5th grade). Registration recommended.
events.blurb: Have grades 2-5 dive into hands-on activities blending math, language arts, history, and science at the Athena Project.

events.title: ELL / ELL Conversation Club for Mandarin Speakers
events.description: Join us for an in-person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English speaking & conversation skills used in everyday settings. All levels of English-speaking skills are welcome! The presenter is bilingual in both English and Chinese Mandarin. Other English language learners are welcome. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice English conversation with other adult learners at this Mandarin-speaker ELL club.

events.title: Trunk or Treat
events.description: Celebrate Halloween with Educational Park Library at our Trunk or Treat. This fun outdoor event features: Cars; Candy [get it while it lasts!]; Music; Outdoor games; And more! Discover library programs and access resources from our community partners (while supplies last). We look forward to seeing you and your family! The event will be in the branch parking lot; the parking lot will be closed to visitors' cars for this event so plan accordingly. Limited parking available on the street - walk if you can! Attention Local Businesses / Government Departments: This year, the community & businesses are invited to participate and give candy & goodies away. Business cards / flyers to promote your business are okay, but no sales please! If you are interested in reserving a spot, please email me at javier.deleon@sjlibrary.org. Free. No registration is required. Costumes are encouraged. Bring your trick-or-treat bags / buckets!
events.blurb: Walk through decorated cars for candy, music, and games at this outdoor Trunk or Treat.

events.title: Community Game & Craft Day
events.description: Whether you're looking to meet new people, learn a new game, make progress on a craft, or simply spend a relaxing afternoon with fellow hobbyists, there's a place for you at Community Game and Craft Day. No experience is necessary—just bring your enthusiasm and join the fun! This event takes place in the library community room. Tables and chairs are provided. Bring your favorite board games, card games, role-playing games, crafting projects, works-in-progress, or creative projects to share and enjoy. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Learn new games, work on a craft, and meet other hobbyists at this open community day.

events.title: Stemmable: Build Your Own Catapult
events.description: Stemmable is a girl-led youth nonprofit in the San Francisco Bay Area that loves getting kids excited about Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM). A dedicated group of teen volunteers from eight local high schools presents free, hands-on workshops where kids can explore, build, and have fun while learning something new. We'd love for your family to attend this upcoming workshop! It is designed for kids ages 6–12; however, younger children (ages 4–7) are welcome too if they attend with a parent, older sibling, or other caregiver. Saturday, October 24, 12 – 1 PM · Build Your Own Catapult This workshop is interactive, creative, and fun — perfect for curious kids and families who want to explore STEM concepts. Sign-ups are recommended. Drop-ins are welcome. Stemmable es una organización juvenil sin fines de lucro liderada por niñas en el Área de la Bahía de San Francisco que se dedica a entusiasmar a los niños con la ciencia, la tecnología, la ingeniería y las matemáticas (STEM). Un grupo dedicado de jóvenes voluntarios de ocho escuelas secundarias locales ofrece talleres prácticos gratis donde los niños pueden explorar, construir y divertirse mientras aprenden algo nuevo. ¡Nos encantaría que su familia asistiera a este próximo taller! Está diseñado para niños de 6 a 12 años; sin embargo, los niños más pequeños (de 4 a 7 años) también son bienvenidos si asisten con uno de sus padres, un hermano mayor u otro cuidador. Sábado, 24 de octubre, 12 – 1 PM · Construye tu propia catapulta Este taller es interactivo, creativo y muy divertido: perfecto para niños curiosos y familias que quieren explorar conceptos STEM. Se recomienda inscribirse. Se aceptan visitas sin cita previa.
events.blurb: Build your own catapult with hands-on STEM guidance from the youth nonprofit Stemmable.

events.title: Hillview - Overfelt Adult Education ESL Class

events.title: Forgotten Voices: Italian Americans Uprooted in Wartime California
events.description: Dive into a lesser-known chapter of American history: the experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast during World War II. Through archival photos, historical context, and personal storytelling, Lindsay examines the impact of Executive Order 9066 on Italian American communities, especially in the Bay Area. Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations. Highlights include: the little-known internment of Italian Americans alongside Japanese and German communities; the devastation of family-run industries like fishing in California; stories of resilience, cultural erasure, and rediscovery; legislation and resolutions acknowledging past injustices. Lindsay Marie Morris is a novelist and journalist based in Los Angeles. Her novels are inspired by her Sicilian-American roots and are grounded in years of historical research, from family archives and oral history interviews to wartime records and on-the-ground exploration in her novel settings. All are welcome. No registration needed. This program celebrates Italian-American Heritage and Culture Month. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Learn about the World War II experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast at Cupertino Library.

events.description: The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) are hosting a friendly needlework stitch-in. Come join us from 10 am to 2 pm in the conference room; there are always extra seats! The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) chapter of the American Needlepoint Guild was chartered on March 1, 1986. We meet monthly at the Milpitas Police Department Community Room. At our meetings we present programs which encourage and inspire members to explore new techniques in needlepoint, learn about design, color, texture and perspective, and provide an opportunity to network with others who share a passion for needlepoint. The purpose of the American Needlepoint Guild is for education and cultural development through participation in and encouragement of interest in the art of needlepoint, which is defined as needlework executed by hand with a threaded needle on a readily counted ground. If you would like to find out more about SBN, please join us at one of our meetings or contact us at: sbnangcontact@gmail.com.

events.title: Forgotten Voices: Italian Americans Uprooted in Wartime California
events.description: Dive into a lesser-known chapter of American history: the experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast during World War II. Through archival photos, historical context, and personal storytelling, Lindsay examines the impact of Executive Order 9066 on Italian American communities, especially in the Bay Area. Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations. Highlights include: the little-known internment of Italian Americans alongside Japanese and German communities; the devastation of family-run industries like fishing in California; stories of resilience, cultural erasure, and rediscovery; legislation and resolutions acknowledging past injustices. Lindsay Marie Morris is a novelist and journalist based in Los Angeles. Her novels are inspired by her Sicilian-American roots and are grounded in years of historical research, from family archives and oral history interviews to wartime records and on-the-ground exploration in her novel settings. All are welcome. No registration needed. This program celebrates Italian-American Heritage and Culture Month. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Learn about the World War II experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast at Milpitas Library.

events.description: Get ready to wiggle, move, and read! Can you hop like a bunny, clap like a seal, or stomp like a dinosaur? They will also show you fun ways to incorporate fine motor skills, gross motor skills, and sensory play in the library's underwater-themed play space!
