events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 1st: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Make Friends and Be Frank with Them "Every friendship is desirable for itself, but it has its origin in personal advantage." Vatican Sayings 23. "We do not need the help of our friends so much as the confidence that our friends will help us." Vatican Sayings 34. "The man continually seeking help is no friend, nor is the one who never links help with friendship. For the one barters kindness for favors, while the other cuts off hope for the future." Vatican Sayings 39. "Of all the things that wisdom provides for the happiness of the whole man, by far the most important is the acquisition of friendship." Principal Doctrine 27. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 6 (pp. 54-65) and 7 (pp. 66-79). Some Questions to Discuss: What are the two main qualities that make a relationship a friendship, according to Emily Austin's analysis of Epicurus's views on friendship? [Austin, 56-7]; Austin says that "a shared sense of what truly matters" [64] is a core condition for friendship. What is the meaning of this condition? Do our current ideas about friendship coincide with those of Epicurus? What do we value in friendship? What is "frank speech" for you? Why can we be uncomfortable with telling a friend the truth? What is the reason for feeling this way? Can we be frank even with ourselves? A friend vs. Psychologist: where does your preference lie and why?

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, TransMilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at SXSW and received critical acclaim. TransMilitary was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows, CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, SideXSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to SideXSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch this documentary tracing a Stasi victim's personal investigation into East Germany's surveillance machine.

The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. Its evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to leave the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Read and discuss big questions about how we live and what we value at Rinconada Library on Sunday afternoon.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Planning and Planting a Little Fruit Orchard

(There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number; Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews; Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media; Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help. You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Learn how to spot holiday shopping scams and protect yourself online at Rinconada Library on Wednesday morning.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into her heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. How does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her novel A Hidden Fate about family secrets and genetic foreknowledge.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: A riveting Academy Award-winning critique of the government's history of militarization, made all the more timely by the current war on terrorism. 1993 Academy Award, Best Documentary Feature. Read the Acceptance Speech by Barbara Trent. The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never before seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY.), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Among the film's excellent reviews are: "meticulously researched" (Hal Hinson, Washington Post); "outstanding" (Betsy Sherman, Boston Globe); "tough.... Provocative.... Moving.... Beautifully edited" (Vincent Canby, New York Times); and "lays out simply and forcefully the case against the 'official' version" (Peter Rainer, Los Angeles Times). The Empowerment Project (EP) worked on this production for two years. EP first came to prominence in 1988 with the release of the equally acclaimed Coverup: Behind the Iran Contra Affair. EP is a non-profit media resource center committed to democratizing the media. Each year, hundreds of independent filmmakers use EP's edit facilities and other services. Since its August 1992 release, The Panama Deception has played in 80 cities, including an eight-week run in Seattle and a five-week holdover in New York City. The film appeared in video stores in August 1993. It was cablecast on Cinemax in the United States during October of that same year. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film but national PBS, however, has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. Funding for The Panama Deception has been provided, in part, by: Channel Four in London, Rhino Home Video, the I. Roderick MacArthur Foundation, the Rex Foundation, the Peace Development Fund, the National Council of Churches, the Car Eth Foundation, the Vietnam Veterans of America Foundation, the Funding Exchange/Paul Robeson Fund for Film and Video, The Charles Lawrence Keith and Clara Miller Foundation, Essential Information, the Vanguard Public Foundation, Lucille Banta, Michelle Connor, filmmaker Michael Moore and hundreds of individual donors. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch the Academy Award-winning documentary on Panama and discuss its themes of militarization.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Read and discuss big questions about how we live and what we value at Rinconada Library on Sunday afternoon.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.
events.blurb: Learn Tai Chi principles and practice slow, gentle movements with instructor Nelson Ng to build balance and flexibility.

events.title: Vintage Media Lab
events.description: Preserve your old photographs, home movies, records and cassettes! How to Access: Check the Vintage Media Lab page. If appointments are still available for the month, click the Book@Rinconada button near the top of the page. Otherwise, check back on the first Monday of the month for another chance to sign up. Each appointment includes a skilled volunteer or staff person to assist you. Appointments are limited to a single two-hour appointment per week per person. Because space and time in the Vintage Media Lab are limited, we appreciate your cooperation in regard to equipment, storage and cleanliness. What to Bring: Laptop; SD Card, Memory Card; USB Drive, Flash Drive or Memory Stick; External Hard Drive; Your Vintage Media!

events.title: Friends of the Vineland Branch Library Huge Fall Book Sale

events.title: Leyendo en español para niños - Reading to Children in Spanish
events.description: Nuestra voluntaria maravillosa leerá cuentos en inglés y español para niños y sus familias. Our wonderful volunteer will read stories in both English and Spanish to children and their families. Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning.

events.title: Halloween Trick-or-Treat
events.description: Stop by the Library for some Halloween fun. This program is made possible by the generous support of the Friends of the Mountain View Library.

events.title: Mahjong Club
events.description: Play Hong Kong style Mahjong at the library! Seasoned players and beginners are welcome. Learn the basics or refresh your knowledge of the game. Playing Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress, and creates a sense of community. This program is suitable for adults and seniors. Free. Registration required. Drop-ins welcome depending on space.

events.title: Native Plant Gardening for Year-round Interest
events.description: One person can make a difference! Come to learn how you can incorporate California native plants in your garden to bring back much needed pollinators to our urban habitat and provide beauty in your yard. Thousands of plants are native to California, and this talk will focus on selecting native plants for color and interest through all seasons of the year. Enjoy blooms, butterflies, bees, and birds year round! Both new and experienced gardeners are welcome!
events.blurb: Learn how California native plants can bring pollinators and year-round beauty back to your yard.

Our quizzes take place from 2-6 PM on the second Sunday of every month, at Mitchell Park Library, Palo Alto. It is free and open to everyone.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interactions with our reading volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading aloud with our volunteer. Please note, this is not a tutoring session. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Meet a reading volunteer for one-on-one or small group storytime and practice reading aloud yourself.

events.title: Saturday Board Games Day
events.description: Drop in for a full day of modern board gaming at the Downtown Library! The group meets every 1st Saturday from 10 AM–6 PM. Attendees can bring their own games to play or jump in with others. Please bring your own snacks and drinks to fuel an afternoon of marathon gaming in the El Camino Room. Presented by The Bay Area Boardgames Meetup Group. Masks are not required in the Palo Alto Libraries, but are recommended.
events.blurb: Bring your own board games or jump into a group game during a marathon gaming session at the library.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One on One Computer Help
events.description: Do you need help using a computer or one of our e-resources? Want to set up an email account? Get some one-on-one computer help with our Tech Mentor volunteer! Our Tech Mentor volunteer will do their best to assist you with your tech dilemmas such as setting up an email account and sending an email, web searches, printing, etc. Free. No registration or appointment required. Just drop by and ask for assistance.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help from a Tech Mentor volunteer with your computer questions or setting up email.

events.title: Tech Mentor
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Need help printing or using Word and Excel? Want to set up an email account? Need ideas on tech security? Questions about accessing SJPL e-resources? From the basics to somewhat beyond, volunteer tech mentors are here to help with thoughtful advice and problem-solving. We will do our best to assist you with your tech dilemmas. Free. No registration or appointment required. Just drop by and ask for assistance.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help from a volunteer tech mentor with printing, email, Word, Excel, or library e-resources at King Library.

events.title: Friday Fun: Moving Eyes Cat Craft
events.description: Join us every Friday at the Willow Glen Branch Library for a fun activity for kids. Activities may include arts & crafts, special performances or workshops, and board or video games. Note: 2nd Friday of every month is free play with Legos! This day we'll be making Moving Eyes Cat Craft! Learn how to make your cat's eyes move from side-to-side. All supplies will be provided. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Craft, play, and take part in whatever fun activity Willow Glen Library has planned this Friday.

events.title: 1:1 Tech Mentor
events.description: Do you need help using a computer? Want to set up an email account? Stop by the Edenvale Branch Library for one-on-one computer help with our Tech Mentor! Our Tech Mentor will do their best to assist you with: Accessing Wi-Fi; Using email; Web searches; Understanding your e-reader device; Using our library's e-resources. Free. No registration or appointment required. Just drop by and ask for assistance.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one computer help, like setting up email, from the Edenvale tech mentor.

events.title: No Wrong Way Craft: Halloween Edition
events.description: We will supply the materials and you supply the imagination! Make a monstrous Halloween craft. School-age children. While supplies last. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Make a Halloween craft from supplied materials, geared for school-age kids.

events.title: Jack O'Lantern Jamboree!
events.description: We're throwing a Halloween dance party and YOU'RE invited! Children and their families are invited to come decked out in costume and dance with us in the Secret Garden of Children's Library*. We will also have fun crafts and light refreshments. Bring the whole family and join us for this special event! Registration is not required. *In the event of rain, this event will take place in the Treetop Room.
events.blurb: Dance in costume with your family at a Halloween party in the Secret Garden of Children's Library.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club
events.description: The ESL Conversation Club is returning to the Milpitas Library! Please join us for this fun sharing experience. Improve your English listening and speaking skills and learn about other cultures in a supportive environment. This program is for adults aged 18 and older who speak basic English. We will be holding ongoing weekly meetings in the Program Room on the first floor. We welcome drop-ins!
events.blurb: Practice your English speaking and listening skills and swap stories with others at Milpitas Library's ESL Conversation Club.

events.title: Music & Movement
events.description: Bring your dancing feet to the Mitchell Park Library on Wednesday evenings for Music & Movement with Librarian Celina. Build early literacy skills through movement, songs, and dance. Instruments, songs, and dance moves will all be introduced so that everyone will be able to enjoy moving along to the music. This program is meant for families with children and no previous experience is needed!

events.title: Reading to Children
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Our library volunteer Ms. Lincy will be available in the children's picture book area to read picture books to children. Children will have fun listening to stories while they develop a love for books and reading. Pre-registration is not required, and children may drop in to hear a story any time during the program. This program is best suited for preschoolers and children in grades K-3.
events.blurb: Listen to volunteer Ms. Lincy read picture books to kids in West Valley Library's children's area.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join us for fun stories, fingerplays, action rhymes and songs! Please park strollers in the Children's room. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Sing along to stories, fingerplays, and rhymes with your little ones at Saratoga Library's storytime.

events.title: Poetry Open Mic
events.description: Come share poetry. Come hear poetry. You do not have to be a poet to attend! Presented by Poetry Los Altos. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Share your own poems or just listen at Los Altos Library's open mic hosted by Poetry Los Altos.

events.title: Halloween Event
events.description: Come join us at Evergreen for a spooky and fun-filled Halloween celebration! Our friends at East Bay Vivarium are going to present approximately 18 spooky reptiles, amphibians, and arachnids! We will also have a Halloween-themed storytime. Costumes welcome! Agenda: 3:30 - 4:30 PM: Traveling Reptile Show; 4:30 - 5:30 PM: Storytime and Stay & Play. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: See spooky reptiles, amphibians, and arachnids from East Bay Vivarium plus a Halloween storytime at Evergreen Library.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join Librarian Jennifer (and Rocky Raccoon) on Tuesdays at 10:30 AM for Family Storytime at Children's Library! Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! While this storytime will be geared towards those older than 2 years, all ages are welcome! Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Jennifer and Rocky Raccoon at Children's Library's storytime.

events.title: LEGO Fridays!
events.description: We have the LEGOs! Bring your imagination and build something fun! LEGOs will stay at the library, so be sure to snap a pic of your creation! In addition to being a great way to introduce the engineering and art concepts of STEAM, playing with LEGOs supports early childhood development because children engage in problem solving, teamwork, self-confidence, and creativity!
events.blurb: College Terrace Library supplies the LEGOs every Friday, so bring your ideas and build something worth photographing.

events.title: Baby Wearing Dance
events.description: Bring your baby and a baby carrier and learn a dance to popular tunes. Expectant mothers are welcome too! For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Bring your baby in a carrier and learn a dance routine set to popular tunes.

events.title: Resume Review & Interview Preparation
events.description: A well-crafted resume is vital for standing out to potential employers. Our volunteer will help you learn the essential elements of a successful resume and prepare for interviews. Gain expert tips on highlighting your accomplishments, showcasing transferable skills, and mastering the STAR framework to ace your next interview. No registration required #sjplworkscareer
events.blurb: Work with a volunteer to polish your resume and practice answers for upcoming job interviews.

events.title: Family Craft: Bean and Lentil Mosaics
events.description: Choose from a variety of beans and lentils to create your own colorful mosaic! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using paper, glue, beans, and lentils. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Design a colorful mosaic from beans and lentils in this hands-on family craft session.

events.title: STEM Wednesdays: Color Me Curious: Dream Labs
events.description: Dream Labs is an art-integrated education program that combines topics such as marine biology, paleontology, and astronomy, with art techniques including mural / collaborative painting, craft projects, and reading books about their topic. Registration required. Space is limited. Recommended ages 5 to 12. Parents and caregivers are welcome to accompany their child.
events.attendanceNote: Registration required. Space is limited.
events.blurb: Make art projects at Bascom Library inspired by marine biology, paleontology, and astronomy themes.

events.title: Knitting / Crocheting / Tatting / Bobbin Lace Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Do you enjoy working with knitting, crocheting, or tatting? Do you want to learn how, see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all kinds of hand needle crafts? Join us in the East San Jose Carnegie Branch Community Room every week. Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting, crocheting, or tatting project to work alongside other crafters and swap tips.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club: Intermediate
events.description: Free. In-person. No registration required. Suitable for Intermediate English learners. We invite you to practice your English speaking and listening skills through our weekly conversation club! Each session is conducted in-person by a library volunteer. A prompt will be given at the time of instruction, allowing for unscripted conversation beyond the textbook.
events.blurb: Practice English speaking and listening with a library volunteer through a guided weekly conversation prompt.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Friday mornings at 10:30 AM for Family Storytime at Downtown Library. Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! While this storytime will be geared towards those older than 2 years, all ages are welcome! Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Heidi at Family Storytime on Friday mornings.

events.title: Silent Book Club
events.description: Join our group and read in silence with others in our cozy fireplace / magazine area. Bring your own book (and quiet snacks), or select one from our collection here at the Vineland Library! After an hour of quiet reading, everyone can share what they are reading with the group and why they would (or wouldn't) recommend it to others. No registration required.
events.blurb: Settle into the fireplace area and read quietly alongside fellow book lovers at Vineland Library.

events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Friday mornings at 10:30 AM for Family Storytime at Downtown Library. Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! While this storytime will be geared towards those older than 2 years, all ages are welcome! Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Heidi at Family Storytime on Friday mornings.

events.title: Homework Club
events.description: Need help with your homework or a subject in school? Students in Kindergarten through 6th grade can come to Joyce Ellington Branch Library on Wednesdays from 2 to 4 pm to get free assistance. Students can get help with their homework / school enrichment or use our Study Room as a space to work on school projects independently. Free. No registration required
events.blurb: Bring your homework for free help from tutors at Joyce Ellington Branch Library.

events.title: Freaky Friday Night Flicks
events.description: Watch some Halloween classics at your library! Bring a blanket and a pillow for a more laid-back viewing, or sit in the chairs provided. The library will provide popcorn, candy, and drinks. This program is for teens (ages 13-18). October 16th: Beetlejuice (1988); October 23rd: The Addams Family (1991); October 30th: The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993).
events.blurb: Watch Halloween classics with popcorn, candy, and drinks provided at Campbell Library.

events.title: Family Craft: Pom Pom Photo Frames
events.description: Create and decorate a pom pom photo frame! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using popsicle sticks, glue, sequins, buttons, and pom poms. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Decorate a pom pom photo frame with your child using popsicle sticks and sequins at the Children's Library.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteers Mike, Sally & Matt. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Hear kids read one-on-one or in small groups with volunteers Mike, Sally, and Matt at Willow Glen Library.

events.blurb: Hear kids read one-on-one or in small groups with volunteers Mike, Sally, and Matt at Willow Glen Library.

events.title: Medicare Mysteries Solved!
events.description: Are you getting ready to apply for Medicare and are confused by the different plans to choose from? Join Sandra Karol, MS, RDMS, RVT, for a monthly workshop and learn more about the different plans that will work best for you and your family. Please register directly with Sandy at isail2@earthlink.net. Attendee limit is 10 people per session.
events.blurb: Learn about Medicare plan options from Sandra Karol in this monthly workshop.

events.title: Seven Trees Overfelt Adult Education ESL Class
events.description: Free. Placement test and registration required. Learn basic reading, writing, speaking, & listening skills with your library for free! This class meets in-person at the Seven Trees Branch Library and is led by a certified English instructor in collaboration with Overfelt Adult Education Center at no cost. Call the library at (408) 808-3056.
events.blurb: Practice reading, writing, speaking, and listening in a free ESL class at Seven Trees Library.

events.title: Arts & Crafts Fun
events.description: Our partner, Budding Leaders, is hosting arts and crafts classes for ages 4+ with adult help, 8+ solo. We will supply materials and samples and help you create beautiful artwork. Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before the program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket.
events.attendanceNote: Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before the program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket.
events.blurb: Make arts and crafts projects with supplied materials at Calabazas Library's kids craft class.

events.title: Wee Love Science: Pumpkin Investigations
events.description: Explore the wonders of pumpkins at the library through hands-on activities where children investigate the various parts and properties of these fall treasures. Engage young learners in sensory experiences, such as touching the rough exterior, counting seeds, and observing the vibrant colors, to foster curiosity and scientific inquiry.
events.blurb: Touch, count, and examine real pumpkins with your child at Educational Park Library's hands-on science session.

events.title: English Conversation Club
events.description: Are you looking to improve your English? Join our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club at Almaden to practice speaking. Two leaders will guide the group in weekly topics. Basic understanding of English required. The purpose of this group is to practice speaking and to increase a learner's facility and comfort in speaking.
events.blurb: Practice spoken English on weekly topics with two group leaders at Almaden's Conversation Club.

events.title: Monthly Chat with Mayor Moore
events.description: Get ready to talk about what matters most to you. Mayor Kitty Moore is hosting a Monthly Chat Series in Cupertino throughout 2026, inviting residents and local businesses to discuss any topic with one of the City's decision-makers. These informal gatherings offer a welcoming space for meaningful conversation and community connection.
events.blurb: Sit down with Mayor Kitty Moore and raise whatever's on your mind at this informal monthly chat.

events.description: The Edenvale Branch Library presents an in-person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. This is a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners who want to develop and increase English language and vocabulary skills. Participants will be practicing a variety of literacy activities. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice English vocabulary and conversation with other adult learners at Edenvale Library.

events.title: Jewelry Making for Adults
events.description: Get crafty and relax at a jewelry-making night just for adults. Supplies will be available to create whatever you like. Make something for yourself or a gift for a friend. Better yet, bring a friend! Not sure where to start? We'll have project ideas and examples to help you get inspired. Come be creative, unwind, and have fun.
events.blurb: Adults make their own jewelry using provided supplies and project ideas at Mt. Pleasant Library.

events.title: Adaptive Activities Programming at Mount Pleasant Neighborhood Library
events.description: Join us for socializing, finding new friends and having fun with art, crafts, and games! Adaptive Activities programs are geared towards teens and adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. Caregivers are welcome to join. Groups larger than 10, please contact us before joining as space and seating are limited.
events.blurb: Join teens and adults with developmental disabilities at Mt. Pleasant Library for art, crafts, and games.

events.title: Classic Horror Movie Night
events.description: Start your Halloween off with the right vibes (spooky)! Join us at the Library to watch the classic horror film Poltergeist (1982). Bring a blanket and a pillow for a more laid-back viewing, or sit in the chairs provided. The library will provide popcorn, candy, and drinks. While this film is rated PG, we recommend ages 16+.
events.blurb: Watch the classic horror film Poltergeist with popcorn, candy, and drinks provided by the library.

events.title: Crafter Dark: Halloween / Fall Keychains
events.description: This event happens on the third Wednesday of every month. This month we are making Halloween or Fall keychains or phone charms. This craft uses beads, pliers, and wire to create colorful and personalized accessories. All supplies and tools are provided by the library. There is some fine motor skill required for this craft.
events.blurb: Make a Halloween or fall-themed keychain or phone charm using beads, pliers, and wire.

events.title: Everyone Can Create: Digital Vision Board
events.description: Using Keynote, students in grades 3-6 will learn to make a digital collage or collection of images, text, and more to inspire them on the go wherever they are! They will learn how to apply an image to text, collect and modify pictures, highlight their goals, and celebrate their inspiration! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Learn to build a digital vision board in Keynote at Rose Garden Library for grades 3-6.

events.title: Insiders: Activities
events.description: Join us for socializing, finding new friends, networking, making jokes, learning to play Dungeons & Dragons, and having fun with art! Insiders programs are geared towards teens and adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. Caregivers are welcome to join. Snacks will be provided. Walk-ins are welcome!
events.blurb: Hang out, make art, and try Dungeons & Dragons at this social meetup for teens and adults.

events.title: Rose Garden Game Lounge
events.description: Come relax and have fun with our twice-monthly after-school game lounge! Enjoy a variety of Nintendo Switch games or bring your favorite games (up to T-rated) to share. Other activities and snacks provided on a rotating basis. Open to current elementary, middle, and high school students. No registration required.
events.blurb: Play Nintendo Switch games or bring your own T-rated favorites at this after-school game lounge.

events.title: Financial Health and Wellness: Optimizing Social Security Benefits
events.description: Join the Library as we welcome financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada of the Heartland Institute of Financial Education back for a workshop series on financial health and wellness! Registration opens two weeks before the event date and is preferred for each individual session to adequately accommodate seating.
events.blurb: Hear financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada explain strategies for optimizing your Social Security benefits.

events.title: Celebrate Native American Heritage Month! Story and Craft
events.description: Join Librarian Jennifer as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month! We'll be sharing Native American folk tales, then crafting traditional clay pinch pots. Please note that while all ages are welcome, this program is designed for children ages 5 and up. Space and supplies are limited; please arrive on time!
events.blurb: Hear Native American folk tales and craft a clay pinch pot at Palo Alto's Children's Library.

events.title: Afterschool Stories and Craft
events.description: Join us for a fun afternoon of stories and craft for children ages 5-8 years in the picture book area. This monthly program will take place on the 3rd Wednesday of the month, focusing on a special subject: September: Back-to-School; October: Halloween; November: Thanksgiving; and December: Santa / holidays.
events.blurb: Hear a story and make a craft with your child at Almaden Library's afterschool program.

events.title: LEGO Fun
events.description: Join us at Tully library every Tuesday for LEGO fun. Bring your creativity and imagination to build unique models using our LEGO pieces. Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards. For children and families. No registration required.
events.blurb: Build unique models out of library LEGO pieces with your family and imagination.

events.title: STEM Club
events.description: Drop in every Thursday afternoon for a new STEM adventure! Intended for ages 5-10, but all families are welcome. October 01 - Floating Frogs; October 08 - Magic Wands; October 15 - Potions; October 22 - Paper Bat Challenge; October 29 - Halloween Lava Lamps. Free. No registration is required.
events.blurb: Drop in for a hands-on STEM activity with your family at Educational Park Library.

events.title: LEGO Engineering Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Come join us at East SJ Carnegie Branch Library for our LEGO Club! Participate in a weekly engineering challenge or make whatever you want! Important: This event is recommended for children 5 and older. Small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards for younger children. No registration required.
events.blurb: Build and tackle a weekly LEGO engineering challenge or create your own design at this club.

events.title: Personal Insight Questions (PIQs) Writing Workshop
events.description: Not confident with your personal insight questions for the UC application or not sure where to start? Work one-on-one with an experienced writing instructor who will help you craft and revise your PIQs that avoid common mistakes and showcase the best of who you are to the admissions team.
events.blurb: Work one-on-one with a writing instructor to craft and revise your UC personal insight questions.

events.title: Learn English: Holiday Fun!
events.description: Are you an adult learning English? Join us for a casual gathering with fellow English learners where you can play games, make holiday cards, learn about American winter traditions, and enjoy holiday music! Registration is optional. If you register, you will receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Practice English with other adult learners while playing games and making holiday cards at this casual gathering.

events.title: The Peaceful Poets
events.description: The Peaceful Poets are a Milpitas-based group of writers and appreciators of poetry. They welcome all who are interested. The meetings are free. The group meets the last Thursday of every month (except November and December) at 5:30 PM in the Milpitas Library Conference Room.
events.blurb: Share and discuss poetry with fellow writers at the Peaceful Poets' meeting in the Milpitas Library conference room.

events.title: Chair Yoga with Patricia Becker
events.description: Join established local yoga teacher Patricia Becker as she takes us through exercises to loosen joints, improve flexibility, improve cognition, and increase strength in Rinconada Library's Embarcadero Room. Registration is not required but you will receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Move through seated stretches with Patricia Becker to loosen joints and build strength in the Embarcadero Room.

events.title: ArtSEE Expression: Thankfulness Cards
events.description: Join ArtSEE Expression's very own Sharvi in this teen-led program where you will design custom thankfulness cards! Participants will be using pressed flowers, paints, construction paper, and decorative accents to explore their creativity through this unique art activity.

events.description: Teens: join us for Coffeehouse, Saratoga's open mic night organized by the Teen Advisory Board and the Youth Commission. Teen performers: sign up at tinyurl.com/TABcoffeehouse to perform. Music, singing, dancing, poetry, stand-up comedy - show your talent!
events.blurb: Watch teens perform music, poetry, and comedy at Saratoga Library's open mic Coffeehouse night.

events.title: Halloween Karaoke Night
events.description: Join us for a night of hauntingly good tunes, thrilling performances, and ghoulish fun! Dress up, sing loud, and let the spirits of music take over. Open to all ages! Registration is not required, but if you do register, you'll receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Sing your favorite tunes in costume at a Halloween-themed karaoke night open to all ages.

events.title: Friendly Stitchers

events.description: A 90-minute informational workshop taught by Santa Clara County Fire Department staff covering hands-only CPR, AED use, and choking relief for adults, children, and infants; costs $15 and participants receive a free pocket mask and first aid kit.

events.title: Winter Storytime Spectacular!
events.description: Join our Storytime librarians for a Winter Storytime Spectacular! Bring home a take-and-make craft kit while supplies last. Follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Hear winter-themed stories and songs, then take home a craft kit while supplies last.

events.title: Hidden Treasures
events.address: Cupertino Senior Center, 21251 Stevens Creek Boulevard, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Join us at the Senior Center for Hidden Treasures! With hundreds of items to choose from, this event is the perfect opportunity to discover unique antiques, artwork, handknits, toys, glassware, housewares, jewelry, and more.
events.blurb: Browse hundreds of donated antiques, artwork, toys, and housewares at the Senior Center's Hidden Treasures sale.

events.title: ESL Writing Club
events.description: Are you looking to improve your English? Join our writing club to work on reading and writing skills. Students will practice writing in real-world applications for home, school, and work. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Work on reading and writing skills for real-world use at the Almaden Library ESL Writing Club.

events.title: Video Game Zone
events.description: Have fun and compete with others in a variety of popular games on Nintendo Switch, including Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate! Open to Teens and Pre-Teens. No registration required.
events.blurb: Compete in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate on Nintendo Switch at Seven Trees Library.

events.description: Join us for not-so-scary activities, a costume parade, and trick-or-treating in the library. Wear your spookiest costume and join the fun! This program is for children ages 0-6 and their caregivers.
events.blurb: Join a costume parade and trick-or-treating in the library for a not-so-scary Halloween event.

events.description: Build, learn and imagine with Lego! Construct buildings and structures with weekly builder challenges! Free. In-Person. Ages 5 and Up. Kits generously provided by Friends of Village Square Library
events.blurb: Build structures and tackle weekly Lego challenges with other kids at the library.

events.title: Chess Club for Kids
events.description: Come learn to play chess, or just play a game! This is an informal and welcoming program. For ages up to 12, and families. Located in the children's area. Registration encouraged but not required.

events.title: Friday Fun: Paper Bag Scarecrow

events.title: Online Author Talk: Cherie Dimaline
events.description: Step into the atmospheric and deeply moving world of storytelling with acclaimed Métis author Cherie Dimaline as we discuss her captivating body of work and her haunting Young Adult novel, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls. Set in a cemetery shed where sixteen-year-old Winifred lives with her dad, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls follows a teen whose attempt to save her father's job leads to a fake ghost rumor—and accidentally summons a very real, opinionated spirit named Phil. Through this eerie yet heartwarming story, Dimaline crafts a haunting masterpiece about grief, survival, identity, and unexpected connections across the boundary of life and death. Beyond her graveyard-set YA novel, we will explore Dimaline's expansive literary career—from the groundbreaking dystopian survival narrative of The Marrow Thieves and its sequel Hunting by Stars, to the dark, magic-infused folklore of her adult novels like Empire of Wild and VenCo. About the Author: Cherie Dimaline is an internationally bestselling author. Her book The Marrow Thieves was named by Time magazine one of the Best YA Books of All Time and won the Governor General's Award and the Kirkus Prize. Her novel Empire of Wild was an instant Canadian bestseller and is being adapted into a full opera for the Canadian Opera Company. Hunting By Stars was a 2022 American Indian Library Association Honor Book and her novel VenCo debuted at #1 on Canadian bestseller lists. Other titles include Funeral Songs for Dying Girls (AILA Honor Book, Aurora Award winner, Crime Writers Best Book, Bram Stoker Finalist) and Into the Bright Open (2024 Governor General's Award Finalist). Cherie lives in her Georgian Bay Métis Community and has written and produced for Marvel, FX, HBO, Disney, and is currently adapting two major projects for AMC.
events.blurb: Hear Métis author Cherie Dimaline discuss her work and her novel Funeral Songs for Dying Girls online.

events.title: Online Author Talk: E. Lockhart
events.description: Join us for an exciting author talk with #1 New York Times bestselling author E. Lockhart as we reflect on her impressive body of work, including the literary sensation We Were Liars, and even gain an exclusive sneak peek into her shimmering new thriller, The Pools. Once, in a small New England town known for its hot springs, something terrible happened. Something that should have been a warning to stay away from the pools, if the stories were to be believed. But no one is afraid of the water anymore, even if they should be. When new girl Lexie meets golden boy Chester, their chemistry is undeniable. She's running from a glittering life she won't speak about. He's hiding secrets of his own. Their connection feels bigger than both of them, despite their damage. One frigid winter morning in that small New England town, five people go for a swim in the pools. Five people, including Chester. What happens there sends shock waves through the town, changing life as Lexie knows it forever. About the Author: Lockhart is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of the Liars novels: We Were Liars, Family of Liars, and We Fell Apart. We Were Liars is also an original series on Prime Video. Her other books include Again Again, Genuine Fraud, and The Disreputable History of Frankie Landau-Banks. She has been a finalist for the Los Angeles Times Book Prize and the National Book Award and an honoree for the Printz Award. She lives in Brooklyn, New York.
events.blurb: Hear E. Lockhart discuss We Were Liars and get a preview of her new thriller, The Pools.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Paul Vigna
events.description: Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today's global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today's secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. Through engaging anecdotes, original research, and fresh perspectives on the causes of the many challenges we face today, Vigna makes a compelling argument that money has no power apart from the power we give it. Whether you are interested in economic history, personal finance, or the hidden cultural forces shaping modern life, this talk is sure to pique your interest. About the Author: Paul Vigna is an author, journalist, editor and speaker, with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. He is the author of Guts: The Anatomy of The Walking Dead and coauthor of The Age of Cryptocurrency and The Truth Machine. For 25 years, he was a reporter and editor for Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal, pioneering coverage of the cryptocurrency sector. He has appeared on CNN, CNBC, MSNBC, Fox, and PBS.
events.blurb: Hear journalist Paul Vigna discuss how money evolved into a stand-in for morality and virtue.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Pyet DeSpain
events.description: Prepare your palate for a vibrant culinary journey with star chef Pyet DeSpain, the inaugural winner of Gordon Ramsay's hit television competition Next Level Chef, as she presents her debut cookbook, Rooted in Fire: A Celebration of Native American and Mexican Cooking. Pyet DeSpain rose to prominence as the first winner of Gordon Ramsay's Fox television show Next Level Chef. Now, in her debut cookbook, she shares the joy of cooking fueled by her burning passion for Native American and Mexican American cuisine. Pyet shows you how to incorporate a delicious range of key ingredients—from venison, dandelion greens, to sunchokes, bison, and native berries—into more than sixty fusion dishes. Family and friends will be excited to gather around the table to enjoy sweet and savory food such as: Three Sisters Salad; Bison and Sweet Corn Soup; Fry Bread; Mexican Chocolate & Mezcal Cake; Corn Silk and Honey Tea; Wojapi BBQ Sauce. Rooted in Fire is far more than just a collection of recipes; it is a movement giving voice to Indigenous culture, histories, and foodways through the universal language of food. Register for this event today and learn how to work with nature in your own kitchen. About the Author: Pyet—short for her inherited Native American name, Pyetwetmokwe—is a member of the Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation and an award-winning global private chef. She made history as the first winner of Gordon Ramsay's Next Level Chef and was named one of Entrepreneur Magazine's Top 25 Private Chefs in Los Angeles. Her work is centered on uplifting Indigenous foodways within the culinary industry while advocating for a more sustainable and sovereign food system for Indigenous peoples.
events.blurb: Hear chef Pyet DeSpain talk through her debut cookbook of Native American and Mexican recipes.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Rebecca Roanhorse
events.description: Step into a sprawling world of celestial magic, political intrigue, and ancient prophecies with New York Times bestselling author Rebecca Roanhorse as we dive deep into her acclaimed Between Earth and Sky trilogy. Black Sun, Fevered Star, and Mirrored Heavens are inspired by the rich and diverse cultures of the pre-Columbian Americas, reshaping modern speculative fiction with unmissable worldbuilding. Black Sun, the first book in the trilogy, introduces us to the holy city of Tova. The winter solstice is usually a time for celebration and renewal, but this year it coincides with a solar eclipse, a rare celestial event proscribed by the Sun Priest as an unbalancing of the world. Meanwhile, a ship launches from a distant city bound for Tova and set to arrive on the solstice. The captain of the ship, Xiala, is a disgraced Teek whose song can calm the waters around her as easily as it can warp a man's mind. Her ship carries one passenger. Described as harmless, the passenger, Serapio, is a young man, blind, scarred, and cloaked in destiny. As Xiala well knows, when a man is described as harmless, he usually ends up being a villain. Whether you are a longtime fan of the trilogy or searching for your next immersive fantasy read, this is an event you won't want to miss out on. About the Author: Rebecca Roanhorse is a New York Times bestselling and Nebula, Hugo, and Locus Award-winning speculative fiction writer. She has published multiple award-winning short stories and novels, including two novels in The Sixth World series, Star Wars: Resistance Reborn, Race to the Sun for the Rick Riordan imprint, and the Hugo Award-winning epic fantasy trilogy Between Earth and Sky. She was the guest editor of America's Best Science Fiction and Fantasy (2023) and a contributor to the New York Times "100 Best Books of the 21st Century." She has also written for Marvel comics and games, and her TV writing includes FX's A Murder at the End of the World, and the Marvel series Echo for Disney+. She has had her own work optioned by Paramount, Amazon Studios, Netflix, and AMC Studios.
events.blurb: Discuss Rebecca Roanhorse's Between Earth and Sky trilogy with the New York Times bestselling author.

events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center, as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages including: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!) Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard); Crafts (in Adobe Room); All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by international Kathak artist Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.

For the safety and comfort of all participants, masks are suggested and room occupancy will be lower than usual. Please visit fopal.org for more information. Saturday Hours: Bargain Room: 9:30 AM – 4 PM; Children's Room: 10 AM – 4 PM; Main Room: 11 AM – 4 PM. Sunday Hours: All Rooms: 1 PM – 4 PM.
events.blurb: Browse three rooms of over 70,000 used books, CDs, DVDs, and puzzles at Cubberley Community Center.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Night Hike and Flashlight Tour
events.description: Enjoy a fun-filled Night Hike and Flashlight Tour of McClellan Ranch Preserve and Blackberry Farm! We will explore the woods and nature at night, learn about nocturnal animals' special adaptations, and test our heightened senses in the dark with games and activities. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. Please wear appropriate walking shoes and a warm jacket and bring a flashlight or head-lamp. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk McClellan Ranch Preserve after dark with a ranger, learning how nocturnal animals adapt to nighttime.

events.title: Watershed Habitat of the Steelhead Nature Walk
events.description: Join a Naturalist and learn about the Steelhead life cycle, riparian habitat and challenges faced in Stevens Creek. We will walk through history and view our ecosystem through the lens of this phenomenal species. You and your child will identify aquatic insects as a measure of water quality. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $25 Resident | $32 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk along Stevens Creek with a naturalist to learn about the Steelhead life cycle and riparian habitat.

events.title: Demons, Creatures and Monsters - Oh My!
events.description: Registration is required. Meet the mythical creatures, legendary beasts, and terrifying monsters that have populated Asian art for centuries. Appearing throughout folklore, stories, songs, and works of art, these supernatural, mystical, and often godlike (or demonic) beings have fascinated audiences since ancient times. Presented by the Asian Art Museum. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear about the demons, creatures, and legendary beasts that populate centuries of Asian art and folklore.

events.title: Drop-in Bike Clinic
events.venue: Bike Fix-it Station (Outside Franklin St. Entrance)
events.description: Come join us every third Saturday of the month for the Drop-in Bike Clinic! Use our tools to work on your bike. All ages welcome. Professional bike mechanic Ryan Murphy will be available for advice and help with: Changing a tire; Adjusting gears and brakes; Identifying that mysterious noise, and more! Meet at our Dero Fix-it station, on Franklin Street. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Bring your bike and use the tools on hand at the Franklin St. fix-it station.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Bird ID and Guided Hike
events.description: The Park Rangers invite you to learn about the birds living in our riparian habitat and how to ID them! Walk the trails to see the environment they live in and maybe catch a glimpse of a Red-Shoulder Hawk, Screech Owl, or more! All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk the trails with a Park Ranger to spot and identify local birds like hawks and owls.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Sink your teeth into the ultimate Halloween thrill. Steven Dietz's adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.
events.blurb: Watch this staged retelling of Dracula pull you into its shadowy, suspenseful world.
